report:
# Report on region.fasta (region_004, 3000 bp)

## Summary
The region is not random or featureless: it contains **one complete, unambiguous protein-coding gene** that occupies ~90% of the interval and whose product carries the diagnostic sequence signatures of a **P-type (E1–E2) ATPase**. Beyond that gene there are no repeats, no mobile elements, and no other complete genes.

## Overall composition
- Length: 3000 bp; only A, C, G, T (no ambiguity codes).
- GC = 52.1% overall, uniform across the region (150-bp windows range 45–60%); no AT-rich or GC-rich insert.
- Flanks are compositionally normal for non-coding DNA (GC 50.3% upstream, 46.6% downstream) and are stop-codon rich in every frame.

## Main feature: a single long ORF (coordinates 158–2854)
- **Start:** ATG at **158–160**, preceded 9 bp upstream by a good Shine–Dalgarno element GGAGG at **145–149**.
- **Stop:** TAA at **2854–2856**.
- **Length:** 2697 nt = **899 codons** (~98 kDa protein).
- No internal stop codons, no frameshift-type anomalies; the reading frame is clean throughout.
- Codon usage is strongly biased in the way real bacterial genes are (CTG for Leu, AAA for Lys, GAA/GAT for Glu/Asp, GCG for Ala, CCG for Pro, CGT/CGC for Arg, no AGA/AGG/CGA), so this is a genuine coding sequence, not a synthetic construct.

### Functional prediction for the product
The predicted protein contains the three motifs that together define the **P-type (E1–E2) ATPase superfamily** — a membrane-embedded, ATP-driven cation pump:

| Motif | Domains | Approx. aa | Nucleotide coords (within ORF) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **TGES** (actuator/A domain) | catalytic dephosphorylation loop | ~299–302 | ~1052–1063 |
| **DKTGTLT** (phosphorylation/P domain; catalytic Asp) | acyl-phosphate intermediate | ~604–610 | ~1967–1988 |
| **GDGxND** (nucleotide-binding domain) | ATP binding / Mg²⁺ | ~773–778 | ~2474–2492 |

The linear order TGES → DKTGTLT → GDGxND is the canonical P-type ATPase arrangement. The chance of "DKTGTLT" and "GDGxND" occurring together in an arbitrary 899-residue protein is vanishingly small, so the assignment is robust at the family level (a specific gene name cannot be assigned without a database search).

### Membrane topology
Hydrophobicity analysis (Kyte–Doolittle, window 19) shows a bipartite architecture typical of this family: a few hydrophobic segments in the N-terminal third (≈aa 108–132, 246–250, 288–303, 322–332) followed by a long hydrophilic, catalytic core (aa ~340–700), and then a **cluster of hydrophobic, likely transmembrane segments at the C-terminus (aa ~709–737, 771–786, 833–855, 867–882)**. This is the expected fold for a P-type ATPase (N-terminal transport helices, large cytoplasmic A/N/P catalytic unit, C-terminal helix bundle).

## Other observations
- **Antisense ORF:** a 519-nt (173-codon) stop-free ORF on the reverse strand overlapping the main gene at forward coordinates **1735–2253**. It has no plausible ribosome-binding site and its codon usage is unbiased, so it is almost certainly fortuitous, not a second gene.
- **Short nested ORFs** (384–536 and 2572–2832 on the plus strand, 51 and 87 codons) are likewise chance occurrences inside the coding sequence, lacking RBSs.
- **No repeats:** no direct repeat ≥24 bp, no inverted repeat (reverse-complement) ≥15 bp, no perfect palindrome ≥12 bp, no tandem repeats (period 2–4, ≥5 copies), and no homopolymer longer than 6 residues (only two A₆ tracts, at 1470 and 2181). This argues against IS elements, REP/BIME elements, CRISPR arrays, or duplicated domains.
- **Flanking regions:** upstream 1–157 bp and downstream 2857–3000 bp are non-coding. The downstream segment contains a nearly palindromic, GC-rich stretch (CCGGATGCGGCGTAAATGCCTTATCCGG, ~2915–2955) followed by an A/T-rich run, which is at least consistent with a weak rho-independent terminator, though it is not a strong/complete hairpin. No −10/−35 promoter or obvious terminator was found in the upstream 157 bp, suggesting the gene's promoter lies beyond the sequenced window.
- The region's ends cut through neighbouring transcription units (partial stop-free stretches run to the boundaries on both strands), i.e., the window was taken from the interior of a larger genome/operon.

## Bottom line
Notable finding: **coordinates 158–2854 encode a complete 899-residue P-type ATPase** (RBS at 145–149, start 158, stop 2854), with the superfamily's diagnostic TGES (~aa 300), DKTGTLT (~aa 606) and GDGxND (~aa 775) motifs and a C-terminal transmembrane bundle. No other notable features — no repeats, no mobile elements, no additional functional genes — are present in the 3000-bp region.
